title: Free vs. Starter vs. Explorer vs. Pro vs. Enterprise Plans | Clay Help Center
snippet:
## Free Plan
Explore the product and integrations available. This is best for people trying out Clay for the first time
### Price
- $0 for 100 credits/month
### Features
- Access to 50+ data providers
- Export to CSV
- AI message writing
- Up to 100 per people/company search
## Starter Plan
Best for individuals. This is for people looking to test out Clay or enrich a few hundred leads a month
### Price
- Monthly(billed monthly)
- $149 for 2,000 credits/month
- $229 for 3,000 credits/month
- Annual(billed annually, with all credits granted upfront)
- $134/month for 24k credits/year
- $206/month for 36k credits/year
### Features
- Everything from Free plus
- Create unlimited tables
- Use your own API Keys
- Up to 5,000 per people/company search
## Explorer Plan
Best for early stage startups and growth agencies. This is for people who want to auto-send emails generated in Clay, call custom APIs, and enrich thousands of leads per month
### Price
- Monthly(billed monthly)
- $349 for 10,000 credits/month
- $499 for 14,000 credits/month
- $699 for 20,000 credits/month
- Annual(billed annually, with all credits granted upfront)
- $314/month for 120k credits/year
- $449/month for 168k credits/year
- $629/month for 240k credits/year
### Features
- Everything from Starter plus
- Email tool integrations
- Get data from anywhere (webhooks)
- Send data anywhere (HTTP API)
- Up to 25,000 per people/company search

### Price

title: Clay API review: what it is, and what it costs
snippet:
The first is the Clay HTTP API: a column in a Clay table that calls any external endpoint and writes the response back into a cell. That is the one most teams want, and it is a Growth plan feature at $446 a month billed annually, $495 paying monthly.

The third is bringing your own API key to a native enrichment, which is free.

| Surface | Direction | What it does | What it needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| HTTP API column | Clay calls out | Sends or retrieves data from any tool or database by endpoint, even where Clay has no native integration. The response is parsed into table columns. | Growth, $446/mo |
| Webhook source | Your app calls in | Clay gives you a URL and a cURL command. Anything you POST to it becomes rows in a table. | Growth, per the plan table |
| Bring your own key | Clay calls a provider | Use your own contract with a provider inside a native Clay enrichment, rather than paying Clay credits for it. | Free plan |
| Clay Sequencer and integrations | Clay calls out | Native connectors to sending tools and CRMs, configured rather than coded. | Launch, $167/mo |

### Free
$0
500 actions/mo
- 100 data credits a month, 1,200 a year
- Unlimited seats and tables, up to 200 rows per table
- Multi-provider waterfalls and Claygent
- Bring your own API key
### Launch
$167
/mo billed annually, from 15,000 actions
- $185 a month on monthly billing
- 2,500 data credits a month, 30,000 a year, unused ones roll over up to 2x
- Phone number enrichment
- Job change and other signals, unlimited Audiences search
- Send through the Clay Sequencer or an integration
### Growth
$446
/mo billed annually, from 40,000 actions
- $495 a month on monthly billing
- 6,000 data credits a month, 72,000 a year, unused ones roll over up to 2x
- Integrate with any HTTP API. This is the tier that unlocks it
- Auto-sync and enrich CRM, warehouse sync
- Web intent signals, webhook-driven automation

- A free plan with unlimited seats and tables, real waterfalls and Claygent, which is unusually generous.

Glean, from the Launch plan up.

Do not buy Launch or Growth expecting an API. Calling Clay from your own code is Clay API access, which the pricing page lists on Enterprise only, and if your plan is to have Clay call your code, budget for Growth at $446 billed annually, $495 monthly, rather than Launch at $167. Teams that discover this after signing usually end up paying for a tier they did not plan on.

title: Searches
snippet:
Clay caps how many search results a workspace can return through the API. These limits apply to results returned across the CLI and Public API, and they scale with your plan.
| Plan | Results per request | Results per search | Results per period | Reset date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | 50 | 50 | 100 per 30 days | Rolling (ages out daily at midnight UTC) |
| Trial | 50 | 50 | 10,000 for trial duration | Not applicable |
| Paid | 500 | Up to your period limit | 1,000,000 per 30 days | Rolling (ages out daily at midnight UTC) |
| Legacy paid (Starter, Explorer, Pro) | 500 | Up to your period limit | 1,000,000 per year | January 1 (UTC) |
| Enterprise | 500 | Up to your period limit | 10,000,000 per 30 days | Rolling (ages out daily at midnight UTC) |

Legacy Starter, Explorer, and Pro plans keep the yearly period limit. Legacy Enterprise plans use the Enterprise row. Moving to a current paid plan or Enterprise is what switches a workspace to the rolling 30-day limit. When you exceed a limit, Clay returns HTTP `402` with a message naming the limit you hit. Period-limit errors also state when the limit resets. Malformed filters or other invalid input still return HTTP `400`. To increase a limit, paid customers can contact Clay Support; Enterprise customers should contact their assigned Clay GTME.
